stories.title: Blockstream refuses the ransom: 'Return the bitcoin' for the remaining ~598.5 BTC from the Liquid exploit
stories.summary: Blockstream said it will not pay a bounty for the ~598.5 BTC still held from the September 6 Liquid Network exploit (~4,000 BTC minted via an Elements range-proof caching bug; ~3,400 already returned). It calls the withholding 'a crime, not responsible disclosure' and will pursue law enforcement and forensics. Liquid resumed trading but peg-outs stay disabled while the BTC/LBTC reserve is restored. Builders should care: it is a live test case for who funds recovery of a permissionless sidechain's backing.

quality.note: Official @Blockstream statement post (05:25:56 UTC) is the primary record; no official blog URL was posted, so the canonical page is an independent write-up. The exploit and most of the return predate this window.

stories.title: UniCredit is weighing a digital-asset custody and brokerage push with a vendor selection underway
stories.summary: Italy's second-largest bank is selecting a technology vendor for digital-asset custody and brokerage, with tokenized products, stablecoins and crypto exposure in discussion. This is an early-stage report from anonymous sources - UniCredit declined to comment and says no final decision has been made. It matters because a systemically important EU bank running custody/brokerage would anchor the tokenization and RWA pipelines already moving in Europe.

quality.note: Bloomberg-sourced reporting; UniCredit has not confirmed. Published 13:47 UTC-05:00 on the Bitcoin Magazine page.

stories.title: Zodia Custody CEO Julian Sawyer steps down to adviser as the Standard Chartered-linked custody split advances
stories.summary: The institutional digital-asset custodian is preparing an operational split, with its CEO moving to an adviser role per an internal memo. Yesterday's edition covered the Standard Chartered custody angle from Block/press; this is a new personnel and restructuring development confirmed by CoinDesk. Institutional builders tracking custody consolidation should watch how the split re-divides the asset-custody and staking business lines.

quality.note: Based on an internal memo seen by CoinDesk, not a company press release. New personnel event on 11 Sep; the underlying SC custody angle was already covered in the 09-10/09-11 editions.

stories.title: Sam Bankman-Fried petitions the Supreme Court for a new trial and to vacate the ~$11B forfeiture
stories.summary: The FTX founder's lawyers filed a cert petition seeking to vacate his conviction and the roughly $11 billion forfeiture, arguing evidentiary and Eighth Amendment issues. Filing was reported 10 Sep; the petition's public footprint lands inside this window. SCOTUS grants about 1% of cert petitions, so it is a legal milestone rather than a market event, but it keeps the largest crypto forfeiture live in appellate court.

quality.note: Filing reported 10 Sep (just outside the 30h window; kept as the freshest distinct SBF event with canonical URL absent from the edition and archives). CNN exposes a date only; noon UTC used.

stories.title: Catch-up: SEBI launches Demat 2.0 - a live tokenized-corporate-bond pilot with digital-rupee settlement
stories.summary: India's securities regulator confirmed a successful pilot that tokenizes corporate bonds in the country's ~$620B corporate-bond market with digital-rupee settlement, with CoinDesk detailing the infrastructure on 11 Sep. It is the clearest state-run RWA pipeline outside the US and a template for how regulators will handle tokenized T-bill/corporate-bond rails. The SEBI statement is dated 10 Sep (72h catch-up); the canonical URL is absent from the edition and archives.

quality.note: Official SEBI press release (date-only, 10 Sep; noon UTC used). CoinDesk coverage 11 Sep confirms the digital-rupee settlement detail.

stories.title: Stacks launches Stack Sats: 1 BTC a month (3 BTC total) DeFi rewards program on BTC DeFi
stories.summary: Stacks opened pre-registration for Stack Sats, paying out 1 BTC per month (3 BTC total) for using BTC on Stacks - Bitflow LP/trading and Zest sBTC/USDCx. Bitflow incentives start 16 Sep. Staking is now live (Genesis Bond era) and this adds an incentive layer on top of BTC DeFi. Caveat: it is an incentive program, not a protocol upgrade, and the payout pool is small relative to BTC supply.

stories.title: Cursor ships Projects: persistent, cloud-by-default coordinator agents for teams
stories.summary: Cursor launched Projects - a persistent agent coordinator that runs cloud-by-default, holds shared artifacts, and can subscribe to Slack channels, PRs and schedules. Cursor reports new users ship +30% more merged PRs and heavy Projects users work 6x more on internal tasks. It is in beta and rolling out. For builders: this is the multi-agent harness pattern moving from labs into the dominant code editor, and the artifact/subscription model is a template for agentic dev tooling.

quality.note: Official @cursor_ai post 10 Sep 21:31 UTC with the official blog (dated 12:00 UTC 10 Sep). Beta, rolling out; the post sits 10 seconds inside the 30h cut.

stories.title: OpenAI details Habitat: ChatGPT's online storage layer at 70M+ RPS and 500+ PB
stories.summary: OpenAI published part one of 'Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users', describing Habitat - the online storage layer behind ChatGPT/Codex at 70M+ RPS, 500+ PB across ~40 regions on Cosmos DB, Nanobase and Valkey. The X post says the Python service hit >20M RPS before a Rust rewrite; the blog documents the asyncio delay, connection pooling and process fan-out work. Builders should care: it is a rare first-party look at serving state for a billion-user agent workload, and the Python-to-Rust path is a cost story.

quality.note: Official @OpenAIDevs post with the official blog (dated 11 Sep). Part one of a series; the Rust rewrite is asserted on X and the blog defers later architecture.

stories.title: GPT-Rosalind leaves research preview: trusted access worldwide via API, Codex and ChatGPT Enterprise
stories.summary: OpenAI's life-sciences model series GPT-Rosalind is now in trusted access globally through the API, Codex and ChatGPT Enterprise, with Codex Life Sciences plugins covering genomic, protein-structure and translational workflows; published pricing starts 5 Oct. It is not general availability - access is eligibility-gated - and the page first shipped 16 Apr, so this is a status update, not a first reveal. For biotech/bio builders it is the first frontier-lab model with a domain-gated distribution path and a Codex plugin package.

stories.title: Cognition ships Fusion in Devin Desktop & CLI: a lead/sidekick harness claiming up to 39% cheaper coding
stories.summary: Cognition released Fusion, a lead/sidekick harness for Devin Desktop and CLI that routes work between frontier models (Fable & Astra) with a cheap lead; it claims up to 39% cost reduction on frontier work held as lead, with a recommended Fable 5.1 + SWE-2 pairing. Evals with Artificial Analysis and Vals AI show trade-offs: Astra+SWE-2 is worse on Terminal-Bench 4 (55.6 -> 50.0) and Vals Code Migration (67.7 -> 61.3). The practical takeaway for coding-agent builders: model routing is now a product surface, and cost/quality trade-offs are quantified per benchmark.

quality.note: Official @cognition post with the blog (dated 2026-09-11T10:00-07:00 = 17:00 UTC). Vendor-harness numbers; some regressions disclosed.

stories.title: Google Research: ToolGrad generates tool-use datasets with textual 'gradients' - Gemma-3-12B hits 83.1 on BFCL
stories.summary: Google Research published ToolGrad, an answer-first pipeline that generates synthetic tool-use data using textual 'gradients' (chain first, then prompt), claiming ~100% generation pass rate. A Gemma-3-12B fine-tuned on ToolGrad-500 scored 83.1 on BFCL, against gemini-2.5-pro 83.2, claude-4.5 Opus 82.8 and gpt-5 74.4. Code is on GitHub (zhongyi-zhou/toolgrad) and the paper is arXiv 2508.04086 (ACL 2026). Builders: this is a cheap recipe for tool-call data, and the comparison baseline is 12B open weights.

quality.note: Official @GoogleResearch post with blog, code and paper. The blog is dated 2026-09-10; BFCL comparisons are vs older proprietary snapshots, not Astra/Fable.

stories.title: Together AI expands fine-tuning with GLM-5.3, Kimi K2.7-code, live metrics and 30-70% cheaper selected models
stories.summary: Together AI's fine-tuning service now supports GLM-5.3 and Kimi K2.7-code with live training metrics, early stopping and dataset previews, and claims 30-70% lower cost on selected models. The company also put a public preview of preemptible NVIDIA GPUs on the same surface at ~50% of on-demand pricing (up to 5 minutes to checkpoint) for evals, fine-tunes and short jobs. For builders who fine-tune in a loop, the two changes together - cheaper models + killable GPUs - change the cost calculus for rapid iteration.

quality.note: Official @togethercompute post with dated blog (2026-09-11T16:00:51Z). Discount range applies to 'selected models' only; preemptible jobs can be killed.

stories.title: Runway lands in ChatGPT via Astra/MCP: image-to-style-frame-to-Blender-to-Seedance-2.5 pipeline
stories.summary: Runway is now available in ChatGPT through Astra's MCP integration, with a demo that takes a product image, generates a Runway-style frame, animates it in Blender, and renders with Seedance 2.5. This is a distribution integration, not a new model - Seedance 2.5 is the renderer. For builders: it is a concrete example of video-generation models shipping as MCP tools that a frontier chat harness can call, and a template for how video-model vendors will reach users inside general assistants.

quality.note: Official @runwayml integration post with a live product page. Demo pipeline only; not a new Runway model.

stories.title: Grok Bot can now search and act inside Microsoft Teams
stories.summary: xAI shipped a Microsoft Teams plugin for Grok Bot that lets it search and act in a tenant's Teams content. This extends Grok Bot's connector set (Salesforce/HubSpot/Gong/Clay/Granola from the previous edition) into the dominant enterprise chat surface. It is a connector/plugin, not a new xAI model, and the tenant-IT enablement path is not yet specified. For builders: agent connectors are the new GTM surface, and Teams is the highest-leverage one.

quality.note: Official @bot post with a live plugin URL; tenant enablement not documented on the page.

stories.title: Skild AI claims $100M ARR, 10 months after first commercial deployment - 60+ paying customers
stories.summary: Skild AI says its robot-brain platform has hit a $100M annual revenue run-rate with 60+ paying customers, ten months after first commercial deployment, with named deployments at NVIDIA/Foxconn dual-arm Blackwell assembly, Sumitomo Wiring Systems and a Mitsui kitchen pilot. CEO Deepak Pathak restated the figure on X the same day. Caveat: ARR is company-reported, not audited, and S1 (the model powering these deployments) launched 18 Aug - this is a commercial milestone, not a new model. For builders: it is the strongest data point yet that robot-brain licensing (vs hardware ownership) can reach nine figures fast.

quality.note: Official @SkildAI post (16:58:52 UTC) plus company blog (dated 10 Sep, no clock time) and Bloomberg. ARR is self-reported.

stories.title: Maven Robotics exits stealth with a $100M Series A for wheeled dual-arm industrial robots
stories.summary: The Santa Clara startup Maven Robotics exited stealth with a $100M Series A from RoboStrategy, LocalGlobe, Vine Ventures and XTX Ventures for general-purpose wheeled dual-arm mobile manipulators (~10 mph, 30 kg lift) doing mixed palletizing and tote handling. Proceeds fund 250 gen-3 robots and gen-4 design; TechCrunch reports Fortune 250 CPG fleets running up to 8 robots on 16-hour days at 99%+ uptime. Caveat: deployed fleet sizes are small and self-reported, and 'world's first general-purpose industrial robotics system' is Maven's own framing.

quality.note: Official GlobeNewswire wire (15:30 UTC 10 Sep) plus the official X thread and TechCrunch (14:17 UTC 10 Sep, just inside the window).

stories.title: AIDIN Robotics closes KRW16B strategic round from HD Hyundai Robotics and Samsung Venture Investment
stories.summary: Korean force/torque sensor maker AIDIN Robotics took KRW13B (stake size undisclosed) from HD Hyundai Robotics plus KRW3B from Samsung Venture Investment. The two will co-develop shipbuilding-specific robots, a heavy-duty five-finger hand for HD Hyundai's humanoids, and surface-finishing automation starting in shipyards. It is one of the clearest supply-chain plays in physical AI: owning the sensing component that many robot builders will need rather than the robot itself. AIDIN exports six-axis F/T sensors to 10 countries.

quality.note: Seoul Economic Daily (published 10:05:30 KST = 01:05:30 UTC) names the amounts and parties; AIDIN confirmed the Samsung leg 'the same day' per the report. No official press release URL published yet.

stories.title: Kinetix AI (Shenzhen) closes RMB500M+ in Angel+ rounds for its embodied-AI stack
stories.summary: Shenzhen-based Kinetix AI disclosed more than RMB500M (~$75M) across Angel+ financings; the company is reportedly approaching 200 people, with a co-founder who worked on XPeng's IRON robot. Not to be confused with the Kinetix Paris lab that joined Runway (covered in the 09-11 edition) - this is a different, Chinese embodied-AI company. It signals continued capital rotation into the humanoid stack between US and China, and into full-stack companies plus component suppliers.

quality.note: Reported via X (@AGkorthos, 11 Sep) and a dated 11 Sep funding digest; no official company press release found in-window. 'Reportedly' language kept throughout.

stories.title: Figure's Index human-data pipeline hits 86,000 weekly active uploaders (CEO post)
stories.summary: Figure CEO Brett Adcock posted that Index - Figure's app for collecting real physical-task video to train Helix - now has 86,000 weekly active users uploading task video, with a live global contribution map. Index launched 25 Aug, so this is a usage milestone roughly two weeks after launch, not a new robot, model or factory release. For builders: the data-engine flywheel (consumer-grade upload app -> fleet training data) is scaling faster than most public robot data programs.

stories.title: Report: Mecka AI's robot-training-data round nears a ~$500M valuation led by Sequoia
stories.summary: TechCrunch reports that Mecka AI - a human-motion/egocentric-data vendor for humanoids - is nearing a Sequoia-led round at a ~$500M valuation, three months after a $60M Framework-led round; round size is undisclosed. The deal is not closed ('terms are not final'), Mecka did not comment and Sequoia declined. It lands in the data-bottleneck layer: whoever owns high-quality human motion data for humanoid training is being repriced aggressively.

quality.note: Two unnamed sources; deal not final. No official Mecka post found in-window. Treated as reporting, not a closed round.

stories.title: NSF overhauls grant funding toward White House priorities - a 'portfolio' model mixing directed Frontier Initiatives
stories.summary: NSF leadership announced a shift from pure investigator-driven grants to a 'portfolio' model that mixes them with NSF-directed Frontier Initiatives across intelligence, quantum, materials and biological design. The dollar split between investigator-driven and directed work is unspecified, and Nature reports anonymous staff fear a squeeze on core science. For aging/geroscience labs, this is a direct change to the grant supply that funded much of the field's core work - and a signal of how federal biology funding will look.

quality.note: Official NSF statement (letter dated 10 Sep) with Nature's reporting (11 Sep, date-only; noon UTC used). Dollar split not yet specified.

stories.title: Sinclair amplifies SRT1720 study: SIRT1 activation improves mitochondrial metabolism in sepsis-related kidney injury (rat)
stories.summary: David Sinclair highlighted a Renal Failure paper showing the SIRT1 activator SRT1720 improved mitochondrial energy metabolism in a rat/cell model of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury; Sinclair later corrected the compound from SRT2104 to SRT1720. This is preclinical only - animal and cell evidence, not a human trial - but it is a concrete example of the sirtuin/longevity-drug pipeline being tested in a clinically important, age-related organ-injury setting. No medical advice implied.

stories.title: Nature: could modified marrow cells rebuild bone? Small trial hints at regenerative potential in osteoporosis
stories.summary: Nature reports on a small trial showing that modified, bone-seeking marrow cells may have regenerative potential in osteoporosis - a bone-rebuilding approach adjacent to the aging/osteoporosis space. It is early-stage (small trial) and the mechanism/population detail lives in the article. Relevant to longevity because bone health is a major age-related fracture risk and this is a cell-based rather than purely pharmacologic intervention.

quality.note: Nature news write-up (11 Sep, date-only; noon UTC used). Small trial; population and intervention specifics are in the article, not the post.

stories.title: Science editorial: no trading on a trial's efficacy/safety results while it's still running and unpublished
stories.summary: Yang & Kesselheim publish a Science policy editorial arguing that no public contract should be allowed to trade on a trial's efficacy or safety results while the trial is ongoing and before the results are public. This is an opinion piece, not a regulator rule, but it directly targets biotech/longevity trial markets (including longevity therapeutics) and would change how sponsors, investors and trial participants handle result disclosure timing.

quality.note: Official @ScienceMagazine post with the DOI. Opinion/editorial, not a binding rule.
